descripcion_geo: Ironic toponym ('house of evil') used by the prophets to refer to Bethel ('house of God') after Jeroboam installed a golden calf there.
importancia_estrategica: Bethel Degraded: The prophetic name ironically describes the sanctuary of the golden calf.

historias.descripcion: The prophet Hosea uses 'Bet-Aven' (house of wickedness) instead of 'Bethel' (house of God) for the sanctuary with the golden calf.

historias.titulo: The battle of Israel against the Philistines near Beth-Aven
historias.descripcion: The Philistine army encamps between Michmas and Beth-Aven; Saul and Jonathan launch the offensive.

historias.titulo: Amos and the sanctuary of Bethel/Bet-Aven
historias.descripcion: Amos denounces the sanctuary of Bethel as a place of sin; Hosea calls it Beth-Aven because of the golden calf.

personajes.descripcion: He used the name 'Bet-Aven' as a sarcastic condemnation of the sanctuary of the golden calf in Bethel.
He denounced the sanctuary of Bethel/Bet-Aven as the seat of the idolatrous cult of the northern kingdom.
He installed the golden calf in Bethel, turning the 'house of God' into the 'house of wickedness'.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: Beth-Aven: relevant geographical region in the Old Testament.

mitos.nombre: The house of God turned into a house of evil

judaismo.descripcion: Bethel, where God revealed himself to Jacob (Gen 28:17), becomes Beth-Aven for the sin of the golden calf: the degradation of the sacred place is the paradigm of syncretism.
judaismo.significado_teologico: Bethel, where God revealed himself to Jacob (Gen 28:17), becomes Beth-Aven for the sin of the golden calf: the degradation of the sacred place is the paradigm of syncretism.
